title: Eval Harness: Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Operational playbook for the eval harness covering prompt set management, benchmarking methodology, quantization profile validation, and a step-by-step regression triage process used by Applied ML and Evals.
content:
Overview:
This playbook defines the cross-functional process for maintaining the eval harness, authoring and curating prompt sets and benchmarks, validating quantization profiles against quality SLAs, and triaging regressions observed in production or CI. It is intended for ML engineers, applied researchers, SREs supporting model serving, and product owners responsible for feature-level quality.

Goals:
- Provide a single, reproducible workflow for onboarding models into the eval harness.
- Ensure prompt sets and benchmarks reflect real production distributions and edge cases.
- Validate that quantization profiles produce acceptable quality regressions within defined thresholds.
- Establish a deterministic regression triage process with clear ownership and escalation paths.

Scope:
Applies to: hosted API models, dedicated-serving model variants, and private deployment model releases that the Platform routes to customers. Excludes: exploratory research experiments that are not intended for serving.

Roles & ownership:
- Applied ML (primary): prompt set curation, evaluation metrics, regression triage lead.
- Serving Runtime (primary): rollouts, canary execution, perf/latency validation.
- Eng SRE (support): capacity for CI runs, observability dashboards, alert routing.
- Product / Feature Owners (stakeholders): sign-off on quality thresholds for user-facing features.
- Release Manager (owner): coordinates cross-team rollouts and post-release reviews.

Core principles:
1) Prompt sets must be versioned, reviewed, and anchored to product telemetry.
2) Benchmarks must include accuracy, toxicity/regulatory checks, and behavioral tests (e.g., instruction-following).
3) Quantization profiles are judged by a small set of prioritized prompt sets plus a broader smoke suite.
4) Regressions are prioritized by user impact (severity) then by reproducibility and scope.

Section A — Prompt sets & benchmark catalog:
- Directory structure: prompt sets live in the eval-harness repo under /prompt-sets/{product}/{version}/ with metadata.json for each set containing: owner, purpose, sampling instructions, and source telemetry references.
- Prompt set metadata (required fields): name, id, owner, created_at, last_updated, intent_tags, dataset_size, sample_source (e.g., prod-telemetry, synthetic), and acceptance_criteria.
- Acceptance criteria example: mean ROUGE-L >= 0.67 on reference set; false-positive rate for policy checks < 0.5%.
- Classification of prompt sets:
  - Golden (critical user journeys, ~500–2k examples)
  - Smoke (fast checks, 50–200 examples)
  - Stress (long-context, adversarial inputs)
- Review cadence: Golden sets reviewed quarterly; Smoke sets updated every release.

Prompt authoring guidelines:
1) Anchor prompts to product telemetry: include the top 10 most common failure modes.
2) Label expected outputs and tolerances where applicable (e.g., allow short/long answer variance).
3) Include metadata fields describing demographic sensitivity, PII risk, and policy-relevant flags.
4) Provide canonical scoring functions (see section on metrics).

Section B — Benchmarking methodology & evaluation metrics:
- CI vs. full-run: CI uses smoke sets (target runtime < 30m). Full nightly runs execute Golden + Stress sets (target runtime < 4h).
- Primary metrics: task-specific accuracy (e.g., F1, EM), instruction-following score, generation quality (ROUGE/BLEU/COMET), and safety/policy pass rate.
- Secondary metrics: perplexity on held-out corpora, hallucination rate (measured via entity hallucination heuristic), latency percentiles (P50/P95/P99) on dedicated-serving infra.
- Quality SLOs (example):
  - Instruction-following score >= 92% (Golden sets)
  - Safety policy pass rate >= 99.0%
  - Latency P95 <= 350ms on dedicated-small variants
- Reporting: every run emits a JSON result artifact with standardized keys: model_id, model_variant, quant_profile_id, prompt_set_ids, run_timestamp, metrics.*. See result schema example below.

Result artifact (example JSON schema snippet, stored as artifact):
{
  "model_id": "redwood/rlhf-1",
  "model_variant": "gpt-style-8b-quant",
  "quant_profile_id": "qfp-v2-4bit",
  "prompt_set_ids": ["ps-prod-search-2027-06"],
  "metrics": {
    "instruction_following": 0.94,
    "safety_pass_rate": 0.995,
    "rouge_l": 0.71,
    "latency_p95_ms": 320
  }
}

Section C — Model onboarding checklist (eval harness steps):
1) Pre-onboard (developer): register model in model-catalog with architecture, expected sequence lengths, and baseline perf on a reference dataset.
2) CI smoke run: execute smoke prompt sets with default FP16 or baseline quant settings.
3) Quantization candidate runs: run target quant profiles (see Section D) on smoke and golden sets.
4) Canary release: route 1–5% traffic to canary variant with hooks to capture A/B metrics.
5) Post-canary full-run: execute nightly full benchmark; confirm metrics meet acceptance criteria.
6) Rollout or rollback per rollout policy document.

Owner for each step and required artifacts:
- Pre-onboard: developer -> model-catalog entry + unit test coverage report.
- CI smoke run: applied-ml -> smoke run artifact + diff report against baseline.
- Quant runs: applied-ml + runtime -> quant report + latency/throughput profile.
- Canary: serving-runtime -> canary dashboard snapshot + logs.

Section D — Quantization profiles validation:
- Profiles are versioned: qprofile-{arch}-{bits}-{strategy}-{date} (e.g., qprofile-llama-4bit-ptq-2027-06-01).
- Validation tiers:
  - Tier 1 (required): smoke set pass for instruction-following and safety; latency P95 improvement >= 20% vs FP16.
  - Tier 2 (recommended): Golden set run with < 2% absolute drop in primary accuracy metric.
  - Tier 3 (optional): Stress set run for long-context alignment and subject-matter robustness.
- Runbook for quant failures: if Tier 1 fails, block canary rollout. If Tier 2 fails but Tier 1 passes, require product sign-off and limit rollout to dedicated-non-critical pools.
- Example CLI to run quant validation (internal tool):

# run-quant-validate --model-id redwood/rlhf-1 --profile qprofile-llama-4bit-ptq-2027-06-01 --prompt-sets smoke,golden --output result.json

Section E — Regression triage playbook (step-by-step):
1) Detection: Regression alerts originate from: CI diff reports, nightly golden-run delta > threshold, production canary A/B test failing SLOs, or customer-reported incidents. Alert channel: #applied-ml-regressions Slack and PagerDuty on P0.
2) First responder (Applied ML on-call): acknowledge within 15 minutes, collect artifacts (result artifacts, canary logs, diff reports, telemetry traces).
3) Reproducibility: run the failing prompt sets against the latest baseline FP16 and the candidate variant. Document commands and artifacts in the regression ticket.
4) Impact assessment: classify severity by user impact matrix:
  - P0: data-loss, incorrect billing, or regulatory exposure.
  - P1: major product regressions (e.g., instruction-following < 85%).
  - P2/P3: low-impact quality drops or stylistic differences.
5) Root cause hypothesis & quick mitigation: check changes in quant profile, model weights, tokenization, prompt templating, or dataset drift. If mitigation exists (rollback, use fallback model variant, or temporary routing policy), execute and notify stakeholders.
6) Deep investigation: pair Applied ML + Serving Runtime + SRE to produce a postmortem within 5 business days for P0/P1 incidents and within 10 business days for P2. Postmortem must include reproducible testcases, diff visualizations, and a regression fix plan.
7) Close & retro: schedule a knowledge-sharing session, update prompt sets or quant profiles as needed, and record remediation in regression-triage index.

Section F — Observability & dashboards:
- Mandatory dashboards: Regression overview (trend of delta against baseline), Per-prompt heatmap (showing which prompts changed most), Quant profile comparison (latency/cost vs quality), Canary A/B metrics.
- Alert thresholds (examples): nightly Golden delta in instruction-following > 1.5% -> PagerDuty P1; Canary A/B safety-pass-rate drop > 0.5% -> Slack alert + SRE on-call.
- Artifact retention: result artifacts kept for 180 days; full run logs for 90 days.

Section G — Examples & templates:
- Regression ticket template (Jira fields): title, severity, model_id, model_variant, quant_profile_id, prompt_set_ids, reproduction-commands, artifacts (links), preliminary hypothesis, mitigation actions, owner, SLA for response.
- Example reproduction command:
  python tools/run_eval.py --model redwood/rlhf-1 --variant gpt-8b-4bit --prompt-set ps-prod-search-2027-06 --output artifacts/run-2027-08-01.json
